description: Forty extreme SQL-writing exercises integrating query construction, filtering, functions, conversions, joins, self-joins, composite keys, grouping, aggregates, outer joins and NULL handling. The supplied course cheat sheet is the authority for SQL scope.

sql-campus-network.title: University faculties, teaching hierarchy and composite-key enrolments
sql-campus-network.sql:
CREATE TABLE faculties (
 faculty_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, faculty_name VARCHAR(60) NOT NULL, campus VARCHAR(40) NOT NULL
);
CREATE TABLE lecturers (
 lecturer_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, first_name VARCHAR(40) NOT NULL, last_name VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
 supervisor_id INTEGER REFERENCES lecturers(lecturer_id), faculty_id INTEGER REFERENCES faculties(faculty_id),
 hired_on DATE NOT NULL, salary NUMERIC(10,2), email VARCHAR(100)
);

 student_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, first_name VARCHAR(40) NOT NULL, last_name VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
 mentor_id INTEGER REFERENCES lecturers(lecturer_id), birth_date DATE, city VARCHAR(40), scholarship NUMERIC(8,2)
);

 course_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, course_code VARCHAR(12) NOT NULL, title VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL,
 faculty_id INTEGER REFERENCES faculties(faculty_id), fee NUMERIC(8,2) NOT NULL, credits INTEGER NOT NULL
);
CREATE TABLE sections (
 section_id INTEGER NOT NULL, course_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES courses(course_id),
 lecturer_id INTEGER REFERENCES lecturers(lecturer_id), starts_on DATE NOT NULL, room_code VARCHAR(12),
 PRIMARY KEY(section_id,course_id)
);

 student_id INTEGER REFERENCES students(student_id), section_id INTEGER NOT NULL, course_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
 registered_on DATE NOT NULL, grade NUMERIC(5,2), paid_amount NUMERIC(8,2),
 PRIMARY KEY(student_id,section_id,course_id),

sql-extreme-001.title: Regional department workload under management chains
sql-extreme-001.instructions: For each staffed department, report its region, manager chain root, employee count, known email count, distinct projects, logged hours and average salary. Retain departments with no staff; include only projects starting in 2024 or later when counting project activity. Keep departments whose employee count is at least 2 or whose project count is zero. Sort by region, then logged hours descending with NULL last.
sql-extreme-001.referenceSolution:
SELECT d.department_id, d.department_name, r.region_name,
       CONCAT(root.first_name, ' ', root.last_name) AS hierarchy_root,
       COUNT(DISTINCT e.employee_id) AS employee_count,
       COUNT(DISTINCT e.email) AS known_email_count,
       COUNT(DISTINCT p.project_id) AS project_count,
       SUM(w.hours) AS logged_hours,
       ROUND(AVG(DISTINCT e.salary), 2) AS average_salary
FROM departments d
JOIN regions r ON r.region_id = d.region_id
LEFT JOIN employees e ON e.department_id = d.department_id
LEFT JOIN employees m ON e.manager_id = m.employee_id
LEFT JOIN employees root ON m.manager_id = root.employee_id
LEFT JOIN projects p ON p.department_id = d.department_id
 AND p.start_date >= TO_DATE('01-01-2024','DD-MM-YYYY')
LEFT JOIN assignments a ON a.project_id = p.project_id AND a.employee_id = e.employee_id
LEFT JOIN work_logs w ON w.project_id = a.project_id AND w.employee_id = a.employee_id
GROUP BY d.department_id, d.department_name, r.region_name, root.first_name, root.last_name
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT e.employee_id) >= 2 OR COUNT(DISTINCT p.project_id) = 0
ORDER BY r.region_name, logged_hours DESC NULLS LAST, d.department_name;
hints: Separate the manager, manager's manager and department's project relationships with distinct aliases.
Count employees and projects distinctly because their one-to-many relationships multiply joined rows.
sql-extreme-001.explanation: The department-to-region relationship supplies the reporting geography. Two employee aliases follow the reporting chain; a third alias identifies its root. Independent project, assignment and log relationships multiply rows, so entity counts are distinct. COUNT(email) excludes NULL emails, while SUM(hours) ignores NULL logged hours. The HAVING clause retains larger staffed groups and entirely project-free departments.

sql-extreme-002.title: Employee pairs with shared project and salary gap
sql-extreme-002.instructions: List each unordered pair of employees who worked on at least one common project, have different departments, and differ in salary by no more than 20,000. Include both managers' names where present, project count, earliest common assignment date and formatted salary gap. Exclude self-pairs and show each pair once. Sort by shared project count descending, then employee IDs; return the first 12 after skipping 2.
sql-extreme-002.referenceSolution:
SELECT e1.employee_id AS employee_one, CONCAT(e1.first_name,' ',e1.last_name) AS name_one,
       CONCAT(m1.first_name,' ',m1.last_name) AS manager_one,
       e2.employee_id AS employee_two, CONCAT(e2.first_name,' ',e2.last_name) AS name_two,
       CONCAT(m2.first_name,' ',m2.last_name) AS manager_two,
       COUNT(DISTINCT a1.project_id) AS shared_projects,
       MIN(a1.assigned_on) AS first_shared_assignment,
       TO_CHAR(ABS(e1.salary-e2.salary),'FM9999990.00') AS salary_gap
FROM employees e1
JOIN employees e2 ON e1.employee_id < e2.employee_id
 AND e1.department_id <> e2.department_id
 AND ABS(e1.salary-e2.salary) <= 20000
JOIN assignments a1 ON a1.employee_id=e1.employee_id
JOIN assignments a2 ON a2.project_id=a1.project_id AND a2.employee_id=e2.employee_id
LEFT JOIN employees m1 ON m1.employee_id=e1.manager_id
LEFT JOIN employees m2 ON m2.employee_id=e2.manager_id
GROUP BY e1.employee_id,e1.first_name,e1.last_name,m1.first_name,m1.last_name,
 e2.employee_id,e2.first_name,e2.last_name,m2.first_name,m2.last_name,e1.salary,e2.salary
ORDER BY shared_projects DESC,e1.employee_id,e2.employee_id
OFFSET 2 FETCH NEXT 12 ROWS ONLY;
hints: Use employee IDs to enforce one orientation for each pair.
The common-project condition needs both assignment rows to refer to the same project.
sql-extreme-002.explanation: The employee self-join uses < to exclude self-pairs and reverse duplicates. Two assignment aliases establish a shared project. The manager joins are optional so employees without managers remain. COUNT(DISTINCT project_id) counts shared projects rather than multiplied rows. Grouping retains one row per employee pair; OFFSET and FETCH apply after deterministic sorting.

sql-extreme-003.title: Composite-key section performance and lecturer lineage
sql-extreme-003.instructions: For every course section, report course, lecturer, lecturer's supervisor and supervisor's supervisor, distinct enrolled students, grade count, average and maximum grade, total known payment, and number of enrolled students with NULL grades. Retain sections with no enrolments and keep only sections with either no grades or average grade above 78. Sort by faculty and average grade descending NULLS LAST.
sql-extreme-003.referenceSolution:
SELECT f.faculty_name,c.course_code,s.section_id,
 CONCAT(l.first_name,' ',l.last_name) AS lecturer,
 CONCAT(sv.first_name,' ',sv.last_name) AS supervisor,
 CONCAT(ss.first_name,' ',ss.last_name) AS senior_supervisor,
 COUNT(DISTINCT en.student_id) AS student_count,
 COUNT(en.grade) AS graded_count, ROUND(AVG(en.grade),2) AS average_grade,
 MAX(en.grade) AS maximum_grade, SUM(en.paid_amount) AS payments,
 COUNT(en.student_id)-COUNT(en.grade) AS ungraded_count
FROM sections s
JOIN courses c ON c.course_id=s.course_id
JOIN faculties f ON f.faculty_id=c.faculty_id
LEFT JOIN lecturers l ON l.lecturer_id=s.lecturer_id
LEFT JOIN lecturers sv ON sv.lecturer_id=l.supervisor_id
LEFT JOIN lecturers ss ON ss.lecturer_id=sv.supervisor_id
LEFT JOIN enrollments en ON en.section_id=s.section_id AND en.course_id=s.course_id
GROUP BY f.faculty_name,c.course_code,s.section_id,l.first_name,l.last_name,
 sv.first_name,sv.last_name,ss.first_name,ss.last_name
HAVING COUNT(en.grade)=0 OR AVG(en.grade)>78
ORDER BY f.faculty_name,average_grade DESC NULLS LAST;
hints: The section key is composite, so match both section_id and course_id when joining enrolments.
Do not confuse all enrolled students with students whose grade is known.
sql-extreme-003.explanation: Each section is joined to its course and faculty, while lecturer hierarchy joins are optional. The enrolment join uses both columns of the section key. COUNT(DISTINCT student_id) counts enrolments' students; COUNT(grade) excludes missing grades. The aggregate condition belongs in HAVING. For an empty section, COUNT(en.student_id) is zero; subtracting COUNT(grade) from the enrolment count yields the number with unknown grades.

sql-extreme-004.title: Project portfolio budget bands and manager coverage
sql-extreme-004.instructions: For each budget band, list qualifying projects, client region, department, project lead and the lead's manager. Include bands with no projects and projects with no assigned employees by retaining all bands and all projects in their range. Report project count, assigned headcount, known hours, average employee salary, and earliest/latest project dates. Keep bands with at least two projects or no projects. Sort by band minimum and project count descending.
sql-extreme-004.referenceSolution:
SELECT b.band_name,d.department_name,r.region_name,
       CONCAT(lead.first_name,' ',lead.last_name) AS project_lead,
       CONCAT(mgr.first_name,' ',mgr.last_name) AS lead_manager,
       COUNT(DISTINCT p.project_id) AS project_count,
       COUNT(DISTINCT a.employee_id) AS assigned_headcount,
       SUM(a.hours_worked) AS assigned_hours,
       ROUND(AVG(DISTINCT e.salary),2) AS average_salary,
       MIN(p.start_date) AS earliest_project,MAX(p.start_date) AS latest_project
FROM budget_bands b
LEFT JOIN projects p ON p.budget BETWEEN b.min_budget AND b.max_budget
LEFT JOIN departments d ON d.department_id=p.department_id
LEFT JOIN regions r ON r.region_id=d.region_id
LEFT JOIN assignments a ON a.project_id=p.project_id
LEFT JOIN employees e ON e.employee_id=a.employee_id
LEFT JOIN employees lead ON lead.employee_id=a.employee_id AND a.role_name LIKE '%Lead%'
LEFT JOIN employees mgr ON mgr.employee_id=lead.manager_id
GROUP BY b.band_id,b.band_name,b.min_budget,d.department_name,r.region_name,
 lead.first_name,lead.last_name,mgr.first_name,mgr.last_name
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT p.project_id)>=2 OR COUNT(p.project_id)=0
ORDER BY b.min_budget,project_count DESC;
hints: A range match is a non-equi join; the full budget interval must be respected.
Project, assignment and employee counts can multiply, so choose the counted key carefully.
sql-extreme-004.explanation: Budget bands are retained even without matching projects. The range predicate maps projects to bands. The assignment-to-employee chain supplies staffing and salary data; the lead alias is restricted to assignments whose role identifies a lead. DISTINCT project and employee counts prevent multiplication from inflating entity counts. HAVING retains the specified bands.

sql-extreme-005.title: NULL-sensitive departmental delivery summary
sql-extreme-005.instructions: For each employee-manager-manager's-manager chain with at least one project assignment, report employee identity, manager identity, senior manager identity, department, distinct assigned projects, known and missing work-log hours, earliest log date, latest log date, and formatted tenure. Include employees with no department where they have assignments. Keep chains with at least one logged hour or at least one missing log-hour value. Sort by department, project count descending, and employee name; return the first 15 rows.
sql-extreme-005.referenceSolution:
SELECT e.employee_id,CONCAT(e.first_name,' ',e.last_name) AS employee_name,
 CONCAT(m.first_name,' ',m.last_name) AS manager_name,
 CONCAT(sm.first_name,' ',sm.last_name) AS senior_manager_name,
 d.department_name,COUNT(DISTINCT a.project_id) AS project_count,
 SUM(w.hours) AS known_hours,COUNT(w.log_id)-COUNT(w.hours) AS missing_hour_logs,
 MIN(w.log_date) AS first_log,MAX(w.log_date) AS last_log,
 TO_CHAR(AGE(CURRENT_DATE,e.hired_on),'YY "years" MM "months"') AS tenure
FROM employees e
JOIN employees m ON m.employee_id=e.manager_id
LEFT JOIN employees sm ON sm.employee_id=m.manager_id
LEFT JOIN departments d ON d.department_id=e.department_id
JOIN assignments a ON a.employee_id=e.employee_id
LEFT JOIN work_logs w ON w.project_id=a.project_id AND w.employee_id=a.employee_id
GROUP BY e.employee_id,e.first_name,e.last_name,m.first_name,m.last_name,
 sm.first_name,sm.last_name,d.department_name,e.hired_on
HAVING SUM(w.hours)>0 OR COUNT(w.log_id)-COUNT(w.hours)>0
ORDER BY d.department_name NULLS LAST,project_count DESC,employee_name
FETCH FIRST 15 ROWS ONLY;

Include employees with no department where they have assignments. Keep chains with at least one logged hour or at least one missing log-hour value. Sort by department, project count descending, and employee name; return the first 15 rows.
sql-extreme-039.referenceSolution:
SELECT e.employee_id,CONCAT(e.first_name,' ',e.last_name) AS employee_name,
 CONCAT(m.first_name,' ',m.last_name) AS manager_name,
 CONCAT(sm.first_name,' ',sm.last_name) AS senior_manager_name,
 d.department_name,COUNT(DISTINCT a.project_id) AS project_count,
 SUM(w.hours) AS known_hours,COUNT(w.log_id)-COUNT(w.hours) AS missing_hour_logs,
 MIN(w.log_date) AS first_log,MAX(w.log_date) AS last_log,
 TO_CHAR(AGE(CURRENT_DATE,e.hired_on),'YY "years" MM "months"') AS tenure
FROM employees e
JOIN employees m ON m.employee_id=e.manager_id
LEFT JOIN employees sm ON sm.employee_id=m.manager_id
LEFT JOIN departments d ON d.department_id=e.department_id
JOIN assignments a ON a.employee_id=e.employee_id
LEFT JOIN work_logs w ON w.project_id=a.project_id AND w.employee_id=a.employee_id
GROUP BY e.employee_id,e.first_name,e.last_name,m.first_name,m.last_name,
 sm.first_name,sm.last_name,d.department_name,e.hired_on
HAVING SUM(w.hours)>0 OR COUNT(w.log_id)-COUNT(w.hours)>0
ORDER BY d.department_name NULLS LAST,project_count DESC,employee_name
FETCH FIRST 15 ROWS ONLY;
hints: Follow the employee hierarchy with separate aliases and decide whether the highest level is optional.
The assignment-to-log relationship is one-to-many; count log IDs and known hours separately.
sql-extreme-039.explanation: The employee-to-manager join requires a manager, while the senior-manager join is optional. Department and log data are optional. The assignment join limits output to assigned employees. COUNT(log_id)-COUNT(hours) measures log rows with missing hours; SUM(hours) ignores NULL. AGE and TO_CHAR format tenure. HAVING filters groups after aggregation.

sql-extreme-040.title: Faculty enrolment and academic lineage report
sql-extreme-040.instructions: Produce one row per faculty, course and section, including sections with no enrolments. Show lecturer and supervisor names, distinct student count, known grade count, average grade, minimum and maximum registration dates, total known tuition, and the number of distinct students whose mentor belongs to the lecturer's supervisory chain. Exclude sections beginning before 2025; retain groups with no students or at least two students with known grades. Sort by faculty, course code and average grade descending NULLS LAST.
sql-extreme-040.referenceSolution:
SELECT f.faculty_name,c.course_code,s.section_id,
 CONCAT(l.first_name,' ',l.last_name) AS lecturer_name,
 CONCAT(sv.first_name,' ',sv.last_name) AS supervisor_name,
 COUNT(DISTINCT en.student_id) AS student_count,COUNT(en.grade) AS graded_count,
 ROUND(AVG(en.grade),2) AS average_grade,MIN(en.registered_on) AS first_registration,
 MAX(en.registered_on) AS last_registration,SUM(en.paid_amount) AS tuition_total,
 COUNT(DISTINCT st.student_id) AS mentor_chain_students
FROM sections s
JOIN courses c ON c.course_id=s.course_id
JOIN faculties f ON f.faculty_id=c.faculty_id
LEFT JOIN lecturers l ON l.lecturer_id=s.lecturer_id
LEFT JOIN lecturers sv ON sv.lecturer_id=l.supervisor_id
LEFT JOIN enrollments en ON en.section_id=s.section_id AND en.course_id=s.course_id
LEFT JOIN students st ON st.student_id=en.student_id
 AND (st.mentor_id=l.lecturer_id OR st.mentor_id=sv.lecturer_id)
WHERE s.starts_on >= TO_DATE('01-01-2025','DD-MM-YYYY')
GROUP BY f.faculty_name,c.course_code,s.section_id,l.first_name,l.last_name,
 sv.first_name,sv.last_name
HAVING COUNT(en.student_id)=0 OR COUNT(en.grade)>=2
ORDER BY f.faculty_name,c.course_code,average_grade DESC NULLS LAST;
hints: The section-to-enrolment join requires both components of the composite key.
Keep section-level filters before grouping, and use HAVING for the grade-count requirement.
sql-extreme-040.explanation: The query joins faculty and course to each section, then preserves sections without enrolments. The composite key prevents enrolments from attaching to the wrong section. Lecturer and supervisor aliases expose the hierarchy. The mentor condition is part of the student join, so sections remain when no mentor matches. Aggregate functions distinguish enrolments from known grades and payments.
